newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's BCP boosts stake in BPA.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's BCP boosts stake in BPA.

text.p: Portugal's biggest private bank, Banco Comercial Portugues, said on Friday it planned to boost its controlling stake in Banco Portugues do Atlantico (BPA) by buying a 25 percent stake in BPA from insurer Companhia de Seguros Imperio.

"Banco Comercial Portugues today announced its intention to acquire 27.5 million shares of Banco Portugues do Atlantico, representing 25 percent of its share capital, from Companhia de Seguros Imperio," BCP said in a statement.
The purchase raises BCP's stake in BPA to 75.1 percent from 50.1 percent. BCP bought BPA in March 1995.

"The transaction will be effected at the price of 2,800 escudos per share, the same amount offered in the public tender offer in March 1995, which will imply that BCP's total investment will amount to 77 billion escudos," BCP said.
"As contractually established, BCP has the right to place or purchase the shares held by Imperio, which may be exercised until March 2000," it added.

BCP said it would finance the operation from its own resources and through the issue of subordinated perpetual bonds, eligible as "Upper Tier Two", therefore avoiding the need for any share capital increase.

"The restructuring and integration of subsidiaries into specialised holding companies, and the measures undertaken to bring down staff numbers, underpinned the strategic importance of raising BCP's shareholding to a level more proportionate to the degree of influence and control that we exercise upon BPA," said BCP chairman and CEO Jorge Jardim Goncalves.
The acquisition of the 25 percent stake in BPA is subject to acceptance by the Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) of BCP's request for an exemption from a public tender offer, BCP said.
Imperio now holds a stake of about 46 percent in BPA, which was Portugal's second biggest bank at the time of its purchase by BCP.
BCP stood at 3,335 escudos, up 91, in volume of 33,750 shares at 0844 GMT. Imperio was unchanged at 1,003 escudos in volume of 1,000 shares.
